title: Permission question shows the whole command
lead: *Proposed.* The permission question keeps a short title, and carries the full tool input (command or path) in a field that `ork show` and `ork status --json` print in full.
findings_note: S304 trial 5 (2026-11-16, run ork-20261116-012801-28aa): the approval question title cut a six-path `wc -l` at `.worktrees/S2...`, so the orchestrator had to read the role's Claude transcript to see whether every path was inside the worktree before answering.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: *Proposed.* An allow decision depends on every token of the command; a cut title cannot be judged, so the owner or delegate either guesses or reads vendor transcripts.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestApprovalQuestionCarriesTheFullCommand` (`internal/daemon/approval_test.go`): a Bash call with a 600-character command has a title at most 120 characters and a detail field equal to the whole command, on the status row and on `run.show`.
- `TestShowPrintsTheFullApprovalCommand` (`internal/cli/show_test.go`): `ork show RUN` prints the detail in full.
- `TestApprovalDetailIsWholeAndKeepsNewlines` (`internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`): the detail is never cut and keeps newlines.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Red tests above.
2. Code.
3. Docs: `docs/design.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.
